paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Solomon says unless the LORD builds the house, its builders labor "in vain" (Psalm 127:1). Same with the city and its watchmen. He's not telling you to quit working. He's telling you who the work depends on.

So here's what that means for your Tuesday. You can rise early and stay up late, and Solomon says it's "in vain" if you're doing it as though everything rests on you (Psalm 127:2). Then comes the line I love: "for He gives sleep to His beloved." I think that means you can put down the whole load, friend, and let the oven timer rest for ONE night.

The second song says the same thing from the other side. "Blessed are all who fear the LORD, who walk in His ways!" (Psalm 128:1). Children, a table full of life, and the fruit of your labor are all pictured as gifts from the LORD (Psalm 127:3; Psalm 128:2-4). So build, guard and work, but do it walking with Him, and let Him be the One who holds it all up.
